name: ClinuxFlowProviderRole
title: ClinuxFlow Provider Role (a Provider's role at their home Facility)
description: One Practitioner's role at ONE Facility, profiling FHIR R4 PractitionerRole — the real split this app's prior YAML never made (staff_role/staff_specialty lived on Practitioner.extension directly, which meant a Practitioner could never hold a second role at a second facility without a second, disconnected Practitioner record). PractitionerRole.practitioner + .organization are the two references that make one person's multiple roles across facilities/affiliates representable at all. Role codes grounded against the real HPR createHprId 'role' table (docs/NHPR SBX Doc/NHPR Doc/HPR/1. Register Healthcare Professional (Doctor & Nurse) API.pdf).

element.comment: The facility this role is held at. For a provider's HOME facility this is their own employer; ClinuxFlowAffiliatePractitionerRole (a sibling profile, same base resource) is the same shape used for a VISITING practitioner's role at a facility that isn't their home one — the distinction is which profile applies, not a different resource.

HPR createHprId: role, Required — real HPR code table: 1=Healthcare Professional, 2=Facility Manager, 3=Healthcare Professional and Facility Manager. Bound to that real 3-value table, not an open string. ("Administrator" as a clinical-role concept in the prior YAML was really this HPR 'Facility Manager' role — reconciled here, not duplicated as a separate concept.)

A clinical specialty is a property of the ROLE (what this person does AT this facility), correctly modeled here rather than on Practitioner itself — matches real FHIR intent for PractitionerRole.specialty. Value binding: the reconciled specialty catalog (still an open item — see SPEC-23's own note on HealthcareService.category vs. clinic-specialities.json's divergent lists; this profile doesn't invent a third).
When this role started/ended at this facility — real FHIR element, genuinely useful for a role that changes over time (unlike a bare Practitioner.active flag).
